problem: Existing instance-level object navigation methods mix different attribute information together and ignore fine-grained relations between attributes, weakening discrimination. Their explored trajectories are also weakly correlated with the navigation target, which degrades memory.
motivation: Real-world targets are specified as particular instances ("whose" object) via attributes, not just by category, so instance-level navigation is closer to practical use. Better attribute discrimination and target-relevant memory of explored regions are needed for this.
key_idea: A cascade of an Object-Attribute Attention Graph (object-aware graph plus attribute-attention graph) and an Objective Retrospect and Location Module, trained with A3C, to weigh attributes differently and retrospectively strengthen target-related memory.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims that assigning different attention weights to different attributes, and reviewing explored regions to strengthen target-related memory, improve instance discrimination and localization.
method: Object-aware Graph (OAG): encodes dynamic relations among all instances in view.
Attribute-Attention Graph (AAG): assigns different attention weights to different attributes to preserve fine-grained attribute relations.
Object-Attribute Attention Graph (OAAG): combines OAG and AAG.
Objective Retrospect and Location Module (ORLM): lets the agent review explored regions and enhance memory relevant to the target.
Cascade output fed to a deep RL A3C framework for policy learning.

setting.backbone: OAAG + ORLM cascade trained with A3C (details not in abstract)
setting.training_data: trained with A3C in AI2-THOR (scale not given in abstract)

results: The abstract claims state-of-the-art results on three AI2-THOR tasks: Instance-Localization, Instance-Navigation and Category-Localization, outperforming related work. No numbers are given.
limitations: Evaluated only in the AI2-THOR simulator, with no real-robot results mentioned.
